a1-01.q: How do you say 'It is four o'clock' in Spanish?
a1-01.why: Four is plural, so use 'Son las cuatro'. Only one o'clock is singular: 'Es la una'. Time never uses estar.

a1-01.q: Fill in the blank: Son las cuatro. ¡No ___ flan!
a1-01.why: 'No hay' means 'there is no'. It says the flan does not exist there any more. 'Está' tells where a known thing is, and 'es' describes.

a1-01.q: Which question asks where the flan is?
a1-01.why: To ask where a specific thing is, use estar: ¿Dónde está el flan? 'Hay' does not go with 'el', and 'es' is not for location.

a1-01.q: Fill in the blank: Chispa, la perra, ___ en el piso.
a1-01.why: Where a specific person or animal is uses estar: Chispa está en el piso. 'Hay' introduces something new, and 'es' describes what something is like.

a1-01.q: Complete: —¿Qué hora es? —___ la una de la tarde.
a1-01.why: One o'clock is singular: 'Es la una'. From two to twelve, use 'Son las…'.

options: Hay una cuchara en la mesa.
Hay la cuchara en la mesa.
Está una cuchara en la mesa.
Una cuchara hay en la mesa.
a1-01.why: 'Hay' introduces something new and goes with un/una, a number or no article, usually first: Hay una cuchara. For a known thing, say 'La cuchara está en la mesa'.

a1-01.q: Put the words in order: sala / abuelo / está / el / en / la
options: El abuelo en la sala está.
El abuelo está en la sala.
Está el abuelo la en sala.
En el abuelo la sala está.
a1-01.why: The usual order is subject + estar + en + place: El abuelo está en la sala (Grandpa is in the living room).

a1-01.q: How do you say 'Xóchitl is happy' (right now)?
a1-01.why: Feelings right now use estar: está contenta. Ser is not used for how someone feels at the moment.

a1-02.q: Fill in the blank: A las doce, ¡___ cien bifes!
a1-02.why: Totals and prices use ser, and the verb agrees with the amount: cien bifes is plural, so 'son'. English says 'that's a hundred', but Spanish does not say 'es cien bifes'.

a1-02.q: Don Horacio doesn't like mistakes (plural). Which sentence is correct?
a1-02.why: With gustar, the thing liked is the subject. 'Los errores' is plural, so the verb is 'gustan'; 'le' (to him) goes before the verb.

a1-02.q: Which sentence needs the personal 'a' in the blank?
options: Delfina pone ___ nueve bifes en la parrilla.
a1-02.why: Personal 'a' goes before a specific person who receives the action: mira a Delfina. La comanda and los bifes are things, so they take no 'a'.

a1-02.q: Fill in the blank: ___ viernes en Buenos Aires.
a1-02.why: Days of the week use ser: Es viernes (It's Friday). 'Está' is for location or feelings, and 'son' is plural.

a1-02.q: How do you say 'Delfina is a cook'?
a1-02.why: Jobs use ser, and Spanish usually drops 'un/una' before a job: Delfina es cocinera.

a1-02.q: Complete: Me ___ tu bife, pero no me ___ las ensaladas.
a1-02.why: The verb agrees with the thing liked: tu bife (one) → gusta; las ensaladas (plural) → gustan. 'Gusto' would mean 'I please'.

a1-02.q: How do you say 'The waiter sees the boss'?
options: El mozo ve a el jefe.
a1-02.why: The boss is a specific person, so he takes personal 'a', and a + el always joins to 'al': ve al jefe.

a1-02.q: The new customers love steaks. Complete: ¡Nos ___ mucho los bifes!
a1-02.why: With gustar the verb agrees with the thing liked. 'Los bifes' is plural, so 'gustan'; 'nos' shows who likes them (us).

a1-03.q: Which sentence is correct for 'She is from Chile and she is nervous today'?
options: Está de Chile y está nerviosa.
Es de Chile y está nerviosa.
Es de Chile y es nerviosa.
Está de Chile y es nerviosa.
a1-03.why: Origin uses ser (es de Chile). A feeling right now uses estar (está nerviosa). 'Es nerviosa' would mean she is a nervous person by nature.

a1-03.topic: Gustar to say what you like
a1-03.q: Alicia answers about soccer. Which answer means 'I like to draw'?
a1-03.why: 'Me gusta' + infinitive = I like to… / I like …ing. With an action the verb is always singular 'gusta'.
Hunger uses tener: tengo hambre (literally 'I have hunger'). 'Hambre' is a noun, so 'very hungry' is 'mucha hambre'.

a1-03.q: At the end of the story: Ahora Alicia tiene una amiga y ___ contenta.
a1-03.why: Being happy now is a feeling, so it uses estar: está contenta. Ser is for origin and identity: es de Chile, es Alicia.
A feeling today uses estar: está nerviosa. Origin (de Chile, de México) and identity (es Alicia) use ser.

a1-03.topic: Gustar to say what you like
a1-03.q: Alicia says: 'Me gusta dibujar.' Cristina likes it too. What does she say?
a1-03.why: To agree with a gustar sentence, say '¡A mí también!' (literally 'to me too'), because the liker is 'a mí', not 'yo'.

a1-03.q: How do you ask 'Are you hungry?'
a1-03.why: Spanish says 'to have hunger': ¿Tienes hambre? English 'are you…?' tempts learners to use estar or ser here.

a1-03.q: Complete: Alicia ___ el pelo largo y negro.
a1-03.why: Spanish describes hair with tener: tiene el pelo largo (literally 'she has the hair long').

a1-04.q: Tinto's paws are white. Complete: Tinto tiene las patas ___.
a1-04.why: Las patas is feminine plural, so the color is feminine plural too: blancas. The color goes after the noun.

a1-04.q: Which sentence means 'I want to find my cake'?
a1-04.why: Querer is followed directly by the infinitive (encontrar), with no 'a'. The 'I' form has the stem change e → ie: quiero.

a1-04.q: How do you say 'It isn't in the kitchen'?
a1-04.why: 'No' goes right before the verb, and location of a specific thing uses estar: no está en la cocina.

a1-04.q: Edwin says the delivery man is not the boy. Complete: — ___ él, porque es alto.
a1-04.why: 'No' goes right before the verb. Saying who someone is uses ser: No es él (It isn't him).

a1-04.q: Marleny has two green jackets. Complete: Marleny tiene dos chaquetas ___.
a1-04.why: Colors ending in -e have no masculine or feminine form; they only add -s for the plural: verdes. 'Verdas' and 'verdos' do not exist.

a1-04.q: Edwin and Marleny want to go to the park together. Complete: ___ ir al parque. (We can…)
a1-04.why: Poder changes o → ue in puedo, puedes, puede, pueden, but NOT in the 'we' form: podemos.
'No' goes directly before the verb: No son zapatos. There is no helper verb like 'don't'.
In Spanish the color usually goes after the noun and agrees with it: la torta is feminine singular, so 'una torta blanca'.

a1-05.q: Which sentence is correct for 'We can wait'?
a1-05.why: Poder changes its stem to 'pued-' only in some forms (puedo, puedes, puede); nosotros is 'podemos'. The second verb stays in the infinitive, with no 'a'.

a1-05.q: What does '— Voy a la caja —dice Nerea' mean?
options: "She's going to the till," says Nerea.
"I'm going to the till," says Nerea.
a1-05.why: 'Voy' is the 'I' form of ir (to go), and 'a' means 'to' before a place. 'I'm at the till' would be 'Estoy en la caja'.

a1-05.q: Nerea wants to know the price at the till. What does she ask?
a1-05.why: '¿Cuánto es?' means 'How much is it?'. 'Cuándo' means 'when', so '¿Cuándo es?' asks about time, not price.

a1-05.q: Fill in the blank: Un chocolate con churros ___ cinco euros.
a1-05.why: Costar changes o → ue: cuesta. One chocolate is singular, so 'cuesta'; two or more things take 'cuestan'.

a1-05.q: Complete: Yo ___ pedir dos chocolates con churros.
a1-05.why: Querer changes e→ie in the stressed forms: yo quiero, tú quieres. 'Quero' does not exist in Spanish.

a1-05.q: Complete: El abuelo y yo ___ a la chocolatería.
a1-05.why: 'El abuelo y yo' = we (nosotros), so ir becomes 'vamos'. 'Voy' is only for 'yo'.

a1-05.q: Answer the price question for two chocolates: — ___ diez euros.
a1-05.why: A total of two or more uses 'son': Son diez euros. Only one is singular: Es un euro.

a1-05.q: '¡Cuarenta años aquí!' How many years is cuarenta?
a1-05.why: Cuatro = 4, catorce = 14, cuarenta = 40, cuatrocientos = 400. The tens end in -enta: treinta, cuarenta, cincuenta.

a1-06.q: Which sentence means 'Uncle Wilfredo doesn't sit with his brother'?
options: El tío Wilfredo no sienta se con su hermano.
El tío Wilfredo se no sienta con su hermano.
El tío Wilfredo no me sienta con su hermano.
El tío Wilfredo no se sienta con su hermano.
a1-06.why: 'No' comes first, then the pronoun, then the verb: no se sienta. With he/she the pronoun is 'se', not 'me'.

a1-06.q: Fill in the blank: Yo ___ las mesas de la boda.
a1-06.why: With 'yo', regular verbs end in -o: preparo. 'Prepara' is he/she, 'preparas' is you, and 'preparar' is the infinitive.

a1-06.q: Complete: El tío Wilfredo no se sienta con ___ hermano Héctor. (his brother)
a1-06.why: 'Su' means his (also her or their). 'Hermano' is singular, so su, not sus. 'Mi' is my and 'tu' is your.

a1-06.q: Complete: Kiara y Joel ___ el sábado.
a1-06.why: Two people = they, so the verb ends in -an and the pronoun is 'se': se casan. The pronoun goes before the verb.
Spanish says 'I have hunger': tengo hambre. Tener is irregular in the yo form (tengo); 'tiene' is he/she, and ser is not used here.

a1-06.q: What does 'Mi prima Kiara se casa el sábado' mean?
options: My cousin Kiara is getting married on Saturday.
His cousin Kiara is getting married on Saturday.
Your cousin Kiara is getting married on Saturday.
Her cousin Kiara gets married every Saturday.
a1-06.why: 'Mi' = my. 'His/her' would be 'su', and 'your' would be 'tu'.

a1-06.q: Yadira talks about her two cousins. Complete: ___ primos se sientan juntos. (My cousins)
a1-06.why: Possessives agree with the thing owned: 'primos' is plural, so mi becomes mis. 'Su/sus' would mean his, her or their.

a1-06.q: Complete: ¡Qué problema! ___ a las cinco para pensar. (I get up)
a1-06.why: Levantarse is reflexive. With 'I' the pronoun is 'me' and the verb ends in -o: me levanto. 'Se levanta' is he/she; 'levanto' alone means 'I lift'.

a1-07.q: Which sentence means 'There are a lot of clouds'?
a1-07.why: 'Hay' introduces things that exist and never changes for plural. 'Mucha nubes' is wrong because 'muchas' must agree with 'nubes'.

a1-07.q: What does 'A las doce, Pelusa se levanta' mean?
a1-07.why: 'Levantarse' is reflexive: she lifts herself up, so she gets up. 'Se sienta' is 'sits down'; 'levantar' without 'se' means to lift something.
Before an adjective (triste) use 'muy', which never changes. 'Mucho/mucha' go before nouns.
Before a noun use mucho, and it agrees with the noun: 'mañanas' is feminine plural, so muchas.

a1-07.q: Complete: Delante ___ la ciudad, entre montañas verdes.
a1-07.why: 'La ciudad' is a specific, known place, so use estar for its location. 'Hay' only introduces something new: hay una ciudad.

a1-07.q: Killa introduces herself. Complete: Hola, ___ Killa.
a1-07.why: Llamarse is reflexive: me llamo (my name is). 'Se llama' is for he/she; 'llamo' alone means 'I call'.

a1-07.q: What does Killa mean with '¡Es muy vieja!'?
a1-07.why: 'Muy' + adjective = very + adjective: muy vieja = very old. 'Vieja' agrees with 'la ciudad'.

a1-07.q: How does the story say 'The sun is out!' (literally 'There is sun')?
a1-07.why: 'Hay sol' (there is sun) is the normal way to say it's sunny. 'Hay' never changes.

a1-08.q: Which sentence means 'We have to go!'?
a1-08.why: 'Tener que' + infinitive = have to. Keep 'que' and use the infinitive (ir), not a conjugated verb.

a1-08.q: Complete: El tesoro es más dulce ___ el oro.
a1-08.why: Comparisons use 'más + adjective + que'. 'De' and 'como' are typical English-speaker mistakes here.

a1-08.q: Julián is nine. How do you say it in Spanish?
a1-08.why: Spanish uses tener for age: Julián tiene nueve años, literally 'has nine years'.

a1-08.q: Complete: —¿___ es tan grande el castillo? —___ los piratas quieren oro.
a1-08.why: '¿Por qué?' (two words, accent) asks why; 'porque' (one word) answers because.

a1-08.q: Complete: Mañana Lina y Julián ___ buscar otro libro.
a1-08.why: The subject is plural (Lina y Julián), so tener becomes 'tienen', and you still need 'que' before the infinitive.

a1-08.q: How do you say 'This treasure is better than gold'?
options: Este tesoro es más bueno de el oro.
Este tesoro es mejor que el oro.
Este tesoro es más mejor que el oro.
Este tesoro es mejor como el oro.
a1-08.why: 'Better' is the special form 'mejor' (not 'más mejor'), followed by 'que'.

a1-08.q: Which sentence uses 'tener' to say what someone owns?
a1-08.why: 'Tiene la librería' means he has/owns the bookshop. The age sentences use tener for age, and 'tenemos que' means 'have to'.

a1-08.q: Lina asks '¿Por qué?'. Which answer is written correctly?
options: Por qué mi hermano tiene la librería.
Porqué mi hermano tiene la librería.
Porque mi hermano tiene la librería.
¿Por qué mi hermano tiene la librería?
a1-08.why: The answer 'because' is one word with no accent: porque. 'Por qué' asks 'why?', and 'porqué' is a noun meaning 'the reason'.

a1-09.topic: Ir a + infinitive: the near future
a1-09.q: Which sentence means 'What are you going to do on Saturday?'
a1-09.why: Ir + a + infinitive: vas a hacer. Don't drop 'a', and don't conjugate the second verb.

a1-09.q: Marta answers: 'Estoy bien, pero un poco triste.' What did Javier ask?
a1-09.why: '¿Qué tal estás?' (How are you?) asks how someone is, so 'Estoy bien' answers it. ¿Dónde? asks where; ¿Quién? asks who.

a1-09.q: Complete: —¡Sorpresa! ___ flores son para ti. (These flowers)
a1-09.why: 'Flores' is feminine plural, so 'these' is estas. Este/esta are singular; estos is for masculine nouns.

a1-09.q: Which sentence means 'This weekend I have no plans'?
options: Estos fin de semana no tengo planes.
Esta fin de semana no tengo planes.
Este fin de semana no tengo planes.
Esto fin de semana no tengo planes.
a1-09.why: 'Fin de semana' is masculine singular (el fin de semana), so 'this' is este.

a1-09.topic: Ir a + infinitive: the near future
a1-09.q: Complete: Mañana nosotros ___ cocinar una tortilla.
a1-09.why: Near future = ir + a + infinitive; with nosotros: vamos a cocinar.

a1-09.q: Complete: —¿___ vive tu familia? —Mi familia vive lejos.
a1-09.why: The answer 'lejos' (far away) gives a place, so the question word is ¿Dónde? (where), with an accent.

a1-09.q: What does 'Este sábado no va a estar sola' mean?
options: This Saturday she is not going to be alone.
Last Saturday she was not alone.
a1-09.why: 'Este sábado' = this Saturday, and 'no va a estar' = is not going to be.

a1-09.topic: Ir a + infinitive: the near future
a1-09.q: Javier talks about his plan. Complete: ___ a pasar el fin de semana aquí.
a1-09.why: For 'I am going to', use voy + a + infinitive: voy a pasar. 'Va' is he/she and 'vas' is you.

a1-10.q: Complete: ___ viernes ___ noche, los hermanos preparan las mochilas.
a1-10.why: No word for 'on' before days: el viernes. Without a clock time, use 'por la noche'; 'de la noche' only follows a clock time (a las diez de la noche).

a1-10.q: Complete: Elena se ríe y abre ___ bolsa. (her bag)
a1-10.why: Su means 'her' (and also 'his' or 'their'). Bolsa is singular, so su, not sus. Mi is 'my' and tu is 'your'.

a1-10.q: Complete: Raúl busca los billetes, pero no los ___. (find)
a1-10.why: Encontrar changes o → ue in the stressed stem: encuentra (he finds). 'Encontra' is not a form, 'encuentran' is they, and 'encontrar' is the infinitive.

a1-10.q: Elena asks Grandpa: '¿___ ir con nosotros?' (Do you want)
a1-10.why: Querer changes e → ie: quieres (you want). 'Quiere' is he/she and 'quiero' is I.

a1-10.q: How do you say 'The train leaves at eight in the morning'?
options: El tren sale en las ocho de la mañana.
El tren sale a las ocho de la mañana.
El tren sale las ocho de la mañana.
El tren sale a la ocho de la mañana.
a1-10.why: Clock time = 'a las + number', and after a clock time use 'de la mañana'.

a1-10.q: Grandpa says: «Es más grande que en ___ recuerdos.» (my memories)
a1-10.why: Recuerdos is plural, so mi becomes mis: possessives agree with the thing owned (many memories), not with the owner (one grandpa). Sus would mean his/their, and mío does not go before a noun.

a1-10.q: How do you say 'I want to see the sea'?
a1-10.why: With yo, querer becomes quiero (e → ie, ending -o). 'Quiere' is he/she, as in the story: el abuelo quiere ver el mar.

a1-10.q: Complete: Nosotros ___ ir a la playa. (want)
a1-10.why: With nosotros the stem does not change: queremos. 'Quieren' is they and 'quiere' is he/she.

a2-01.q: Fill in the blanks: El sábado Ana ___ tarde a la estación y después ___ por el andén.
a2-01.why: Ana is 'she': -ar verbs take -ó (llegó) and -er verbs take -ió (corrió). Llegió and corró mix up the two endings; llegué and corrí are the 'I' forms.

a2-01.q: Which sentence correctly says 'Ana saw a message and said "What luck!"'?
options: Ana vió un mensaje y dijo: «¡Qué suerte!».
Ana vio un mensaje y dició: «¡Qué suerte!».
Ana vio un mensaje y dijo: «¡Qué suerte!».
Ana veyó un mensaje y dijo: «¡Qué suerte!».
a2-01.why: Ver gives vio, with no written accent (like dio and fue). Decir has the irregular stem dij- and ends in plain -o: dijo, not dició. Veyó doesn't exist.

a2-01.topic: Ir a + infinitive, and ir a + place
a2-01.q: What does 'Voy a llegar primero' mean, compared with 'Voy a Valencia'?
options: Both are future plans with a verb after 'a'.
Both mean that I already went somewhere.
The first is a destination; the second is a future plan.
The first is a future plan (I'm going to arrive first); the second is a destination (I'm going to Valencia).
a2-01.why: After a, an infinitive (llegar) signals a near-future plan, while a place (Valencia) tells you where you are going.

a2-01.q: Pablo says he bought two bus tickets yesterday. Fill in the blank: Ayer ___ dos billetes de autobús.
a2-01.why: For yo, -ar verbs end in -é with a written accent: compré. Compró is he/she, -í is the yo ending for -er/-ir verbs, and compre without the accent is not the preterite.

a2-01.q: Which sentence has a mistake in the preterite?
options: Ana y Pablo llegaron a Valencia.
a2-01.why: Subir is an -ir verb, so the 'they' form ends in -ieron: subieron. The -aron ending is only for -ar verbs (llegaron).

a2-01.q: Fill in the blank: Los padres de Ana ___ que el tren tenía una avería.
a2-01.why: After the j of the stem dij-, the 'they' ending is -eron, not -ieron: dijeron. Decir never uses a regular stem in the preterite, so decieron is wrong.

a2-01.topic: Ir a + infinitive, and ir a + place
a2-01.q: Fill in the blank: Mañana yo ___ tocar la guitarra en la boda.
a2-01.why: The near future is ir + a + infinitive: voy a tocar. 'Voy tocar' drops the a, va a is the wrong person, and al (a + el) only goes before a masculine noun: voy al pueblo.

a2-01.topic: Ir a + infinitive, and ir a + place
a2-01.q: Fill in the blank: Ana y Pablo van ___ pueblo.
a2-01.why: A destination takes ir a + place, and a + el always becomes al: van al pueblo. 'A el' is never written, pueblo is masculine (not a la), and ir uses a, not en, for where you are going.

a2-02.q: The note in the box tells Sofía to go to the market. Which tú command completes it? 'Primero, ___ al mercado.'
a2-02.why: Ir has an irregular tú command: ve. Va and vas are present-tense statements ('goes', 'you go'), and ves comes from ver ('you see').

a2-02.topic: Object pronouns: le dio, te lo regala
a2-02.q: In 'Ella te lo regala', what does lo stand for, and why does te come first?
options: Lo is the thing given (the puppy); te is the person receiving, and the indirect pronoun always goes first.
Lo means 'to him', so it should really go before te.
Lo is the person receiving; te is the thing given.
Lo is the puppy, but the order is free, so 'lo te regala' is also correct.
a2-02.why: With two pronouns, the indirect one (to whom: te) goes first and the direct one (what: lo = el cachorro) second: te lo = it to you. 'Lo te' is never correct.

a2-02.q: Put the story events in order: 'Entonces, el perro saltó a sus brazos. Primero, Sofía abrió la caja. Después, corrió por la calle.'
options: Después, corrió por la calle. Primero, abrió la caja. Entonces, el perro saltó.
Primero, el perro saltó. Entonces, abrió la caja. Después, corrió.
Primero, Sofía abrió la caja. Después, corrió por la calle. Entonces, el perro saltó.
Entonces, el perro saltó. Después, corrió. Primero, abrió la caja.
a2-02.why: Primero starts the sequence, después (afterwards) continues it, and entonces (then, at that moment) introduces what happened next.

a2-02.topic: Object pronouns: le dio, te lo regala
a2-02.q: In 'El panadero tomó los mangos y le dio un pan dulce', who receives the sweet bread?
a2-02.why: Le is the indirect object pronoun: it shows who receives (to her). In the story the baker gives the sweet bread to Sofía; le never refers to the subject (the baker).

a2-02.q: Turn the statement into a tú command for Sofía: 'Sofía lleva los mangos a la panadería' > '___ los mangos a la panadería, Sofía.'
a2-02.why: For regular verbs, the tú command looks like the he/she present: lleva. Llevas is a statement ('you take'), lleve is the formal usted command, and llevar is the infinitive.

a2-02.topic: Object pronouns: le dio, te lo regala
a2-02.q: Fill in the blank: Doña Fabiola ___ dio una bolsa de mangos (a Sofía).
a2-02.why: Sofía receives the bag, so she is the indirect object: le = to her. La would make Sofía the thing given, and se is not used alone here.

a2-02.q: Fill in the blank: El abuelo llegó a las nueve ___ mañana.
a2-02.why: After a clock time, Spanish uses de la mañana (at nine in the morning). Without a clock time it's por la mañana: Por la mañana, el abuelo llegó.

a2-02.q: What is the tú command of venir (to come)?
a2-02.why: Venir has a short irregular tú command: ven (like ve, pon, sal). Vienes and viene are statements, and venga is the formal usted command.

a2-03.topic: Irregular preterite: fue, puso, hice, dijo
a2-03.q: Fill in the blank: Abuela, ayer yo ___ tu receta.
a2-03.why: Hacer has the irregular stem hic-, and the yo form ends in -e with no accent: hice. Hizo is he/she (c becomes z); hací and hicé don't exist.

a2-03.q: Mateo tastes the dish (el plato) he has just cooked. How does he say 'It tastes good'?
a2-03.why: Estar describes how food tastes as you experience it: está rico. Es rico would describe a general quality (and with a person, ser rico means 'to be rich'). Hay means 'there is'.

a2-03.topic: Irregular preterite: fue, puso, hice, dijo
a2-03.q: Fill in the blank: —___ que tomar el autobús de las seis —dijo la abuela.
a2-03.why: Tener has the irregular preterite stem tuv-, and the yo form ends in -e with no accent: tuve. Tuvo is he/she; tení and tuvé don't exist.

a2-03.q: Mateo's mother tastes the dish and says '¡Me encanta!'. What does she mean?
a2-03.why: Encantar works like gustar: the dish is the subject and me shows who loves it. Me encanta = I love it (lit. it delights me).

a2-03.topic: Irregular preterite: fue, puso, hice, dijo
options: Mateo puso aceite en la sartén.
a2-03.why: Irregular preterites never take a written accent: hizo, puso, dijo, fue. 'Hizó' is wrong.

a2-03.q: Fill in the blanks: —¿Dónde ___ la receta? —En el cuaderno. ___ una receta muy vieja.
a2-03.why: Location uses estar (¿Dónde está?), and saying what something is (identity) uses ser: Es una receta muy vieja.

a2-03.q: Fill in the blank: Para la receta, ___ dos ingredientes.
a2-03.why: Faltar works like gustar: the missing things are the subject, so the verb agrees with them. Dos ingredientes is plural, so faltan; falta is for one thing (falta algo).

a2-03.q: Fill in the blank: A Mateo le ___ los tomates.
a2-03.why: With encantar the verb agrees with the thing that is loved. Los tomates is plural, so encantan; le shows the person (to Mateo).

a2-04.q: Which sentence describes a childhood habit?
options: Todos los días jugaba al fútbol en la calle.
Ayer jugó al fútbol en la calle.
Jugué una vez al fútbol en la calle.
Va a jugar al fútbol en la calle.
a2-04.why: The imperfect (jugaba) with todos los días describes a regular habit in the past. Jugó and jugué are single events, and va a jugar is the future.

a2-04.q: Fill in the blank: Faltaban dos minutos cuando el árbitro ___ un penalti.
a2-04.why: The referee's whistle is the event that interrupts the background (faltaban dos minutos), so it takes the preterite: pitó.

a2-04.q: Fill in the blank: Todos ___ a los dos hermanos.
a2-04.why: People take conocer, with a before the person: conocían a los dos hermanos. Saber is for facts, and todos is plural, so the singular forms conocía and sabía don't fit.

a2-04.q: Fill in the blanks: Tomás ___ adónde va a tirar Natalia porque ___ muy bien a su hermana.
a2-04.why: Where she will kick is a fact, so saber: sabe adónde. Knowing a person is conocer: conoce a su hermana.

a2-04.q: Fill in the blank: Cuando Tomás ___ pequeño, vivía en Medellín.
a2-04.why: Describing a stage of life (cuando era pequeño) is background, so it takes the imperfect of ser: era. Fue and estuvo present it as a finished event, and es is present.

a2-04.q: Natalia asks Tomás: '¿Cómo lo supiste?' What does she mean?
options: How did you use to know it?
How did you find out (know) it?
a2-04.why: Supiste is the irregular preterite of saber (stem sup-). In the preterite, saber means 'found out' or 'knew' at that moment.

a2-04.q: Which sentence correctly says 'Tomás was very nervous, but he remembered something'?
options: Tomás estuvo muy nervioso, pero recordaba algo.
Tomás fue muy nervioso, pero recordó algo.
Tomás estaba muy nervioso, pero recordó algo.
Tomás está muy nervioso, pero recordó algo.
a2-04.why: His nervousness is the background (imperfect of estar: estaba), and remembering is the event (preterite: recordó). Ser is not used for a temporary feeling.

a2-04.q: Fill in the blank: Cuando eran pequeños, Natalia siempre ___ el balón a la izquierda.
a2-04.why: Siempre and cuando eran pequeños describe a past habit, so the imperfect: tiraba. Tiró is a single event, tira is present and va a tirar is future.

a2-05.q: Which sentence sets the scene (weather and time) at the start of a story?
options: Llovió mucho y fue de noche.
Va a llover y es de noche.
Llovía mucho y era de noche.
a2-05.why: Weather and time of day are background, so the imperfect is used: llovía, era. Llovió and fue present them as completed events.

a2-05.q: How do you say 'I was working' (at that moment)?
a2-05.why: Imperfect of estar + gerund (-ando) describes an action in progress at a past moment. Trabajado is the participle.

a2-05.q: Lisandro writes to a stranger. Which is the most polite way to ask for help?
a2-05.why: The conditional softens a request: ¿Me podría ayudar? = Could you help me? The other options are orders or demands.

a2-05.q: What does '¿Te gustaría cenar con nosotros?' mean?
options: Did you like having dinner with us?
Would you like to have dinner with us?
Do you have to have dinner with us?
a2-05.why: Gustaría is the conditional of gustar: ¿Te gustaría...? = Would you like...? It is a polite invitation, not a past event (gustó) or an obligation (tener que).

a2-05.q: Fill in the blank: Ella vivía en el número 7, y en la calle ___ un chico con una mochila roja.
a2-05.why: Había (the past of hay) introduces what existed in the scene: 'there was'. It stays singular even with plural nouns, era can't mean 'there was', and hay is present.

a2-05.q: What does 'La mamá de Lisandro bajó corriendo' mean?
options: Lisandro's mother used to run downstairs every day.
Lisandro's mother got out of the car and stopped running.
Lisandro's mother got out of the car in a hurry (running).
Lisandro's mother is going to run.
a2-05.why: A gerund after a movement verb says how the action was done: bajó corriendo = she got out running, in a hurry. Bajó is one preterite event, not a habit.

a2-05.q: Fill in the blank: ___ pedir unas empanadas. (We could order some empanadas.)
a2-05.why: The conditional of poder uses the short stem podr- + -íamos: podríamos = we could. Podemos is 'we can', pudimos is preterite, and poderíamos doesn't exist.

a2-05.q: Fill in the blank: Ahora estoy ___ solo en la calle.
a2-05.why: Estar + gerund (-ando) describes an action in progress right now: estoy esperando. Esperado is the participle, and espero/esperar can't follow estoy.

a2-06.q: How do you say 'Try it' (la bombilla) as a tú command?
a2-06.why: An affirmative command attaches the pronoun to the end, and a written accent keeps the stress on prue-: pruébala. La prueba means 'she tries it' (or 'the test').

a2-06.topic: Por vs para: por la tarde, para ti
a2-06.q: Don Rafael gives Camila a bulb. Fill in the blank: Es ___ ti.
a2-06.why: Para marks the person who receives something: es para ti = it's for you. Por ti would mean 'because of you'.

a2-06.topic: Por vs para: por la tarde, para ti
a2-06.why: Parts of the day take por: por la mañana, por la tarde, por la noche.

a2-06.q: What does 'Esta lámpara te dará luz' mean?
options: This lamp will give you light.
This lamp is giving you light.
This lamp gives you no light.
a2-06.why: Dará is the simple future of dar (dar + á): it will give. Te comes before the verb.
Di is the irregular tú command of decir; me (to me) and lo (it) attach to the end, indirect first: dímelo. 'Give it to me' would be dámelo.

a2-06.topic: Por vs para: por la tarde, para ti
a2-06.q: In 'Vamos a subir todo por la escalera', what does por show?
options: the way they move: up the stairs
a2-06.why: Por is used for movement through or along a place: por la escalera = up/by the stairs.

a2-06.q: Fill in the blank (I will be): Aquí ___ feliz.
a2-06.why: The future adds -é to the whole infinitive: ser > seré. Soy is present and era is imperfect.

a2-06.q: Which sentence is a plan with ir a + infinitive, not the simple future?
options: Voy a comprar una ahora mismo.
a2-06.why: Voy a comprar is ir a + infinitive, the usual way to talk about a plan. Dará, estaré and seré are simple future forms.

a2-07.q: Fill in the blank: Todas las tardes Rodrigo tocaba la guitarra, pero un jueves se ___ una cuerda.
a2-07.why: The routine is imperfect (tocaba), and the one-time event on a Thursday is preterite: se rompió.

a2-07.q: Rodrigo showed the guitar to Ernesto. Which is correct, replacing 'la guitarra' with a pronoun?
a2-07.why: Le becomes se before lo/la, the indirect pronoun comes first, and la is feminine to match la guitarra.

a2-07.q: Fill in the blank: Es muy bonita, pero es más vieja que ___.
a2-07.why: After que in a comparison, use the subject pronoun: más vieja que yo (older than me / than I am). Mí is only used after prepositions such as para (para mí).

a2-07.q: Rodrigo says to Ernesto: 'Quiero pagártelo.' What do te and lo mean?
options: te = the shop, lo = the money
te = Ernesto (to you), lo = it (the new string)
a2-07.why: Pronouns can attach to an infinitive, indirect first: pagar + te (to you, Ernesto) + lo (it, the string): I want to pay you for it.

a2-07.q: Which time phrase goes with the imperfect in this story?
a2-07.why: Todas las tardes describes a routine, so it goes with the imperfect (tocaba). The others point to one moment and go with the preterite.

a2-07.q: In 'Ernesto le cambió la cuerda', who or what is le?
options: Rodrigo: Ernesto changed the string for him
a2-07.why: Le is an indirect pronoun: the person who benefits (for him = Rodrigo). The string is the direct object, la cuerda.

a2-07.q: Which sentence correctly says 'Julieta is his best student'?
options: Julieta es mejor alumna que él.
Julieta es su más buena alumna.
Julieta es su alumna más mejor.
a2-07.why: Bueno has the irregular form mejor; with a possessive it means 'best': su mejor alumna. 'Más buena' and 'más mejor' are wrong here.

a2-07.q: Fill in the blank: Julieta nunca hablaba, pero siempre ___ un poquito.
a2-07.why: Siempre and the habit in the sentence (nunca hablaba) call for the imperfect: bailaba.

a2-08.q: How do you say 'They didn't see anybody'?
a2-08.why: When nadie comes after the verb, no goes before the verb: no vieron a nadie. The a is needed because nadie is a person they see.

a2-08.topic: Obligation: hay que, tener que, deber
a2-08.q: What does 'Si hay niebla, hay que caminar despacio' mean?
options: If there is fog, there is a slow path.
If there is fog, you can't walk.
If there is fog, he walked slowly.
If there is fog, you have to walk slowly.
a2-08.why: Hay que + infinitive is a general obligation: one has to / you have to walk slowly.

a2-08.q: The woman says to Valeria and Andrés: '___ son los turistas.' Which word fits?
a2-08.why: Two people, so plural 'you'. In Colombia that is ustedes, with the they-form son. Vosotros (sois) is only used in Spain.

a2-08.topic: Obligation: hay que, tener que, deber
a2-08.q: Fill in the blank (we): ¿Qué ___ que hacer?
a2-08.why: Tener que is for a specific person and changes: nosotros tenemos que. Deber does not take que, and hay que does not take a person.

a2-08.q: Fill in the blank: Andrés dice: «No veo ___».
a2-08.why: Nada = nothing (things); nadie = nobody (people). With no before the verb, Spanish uses nada, not algo.

a2-08.q: Why is there no 'no' in 'Nadie respondió'?
options: Because it is in the preterite.
Because nadie comes before the verb.
It's a mistake; it should be 'Nadie no respondió'.
a2-08.why: When the negative word starts the sentence, it is enough on its own: Nadie respondió. After the verb you need no: No respondió nadie.

a2-08.q: In 'Jairo los está buscando', who are los?
a2-08.why: The woman is talking to Valeria and Andrés, so los means 'you all': Jairo is looking for you.

a2-08.topic: Obligation: hay que, tener que, deber
a2-08.q: Which sentence correctly says 'You must follow the river' to one friend?
a2-08.why: Deber + infinitive, with no que and no a: debes seguir. Hay que is followed by an infinitive, not a conjugated verb.

a2-09.q: How do you say 'I have never been late'?
a2-09.why: Present perfect = he + participle (-ado for -ar verbs): he llegado. Nunca goes before he, and nothing goes between he and the participle. Llegando is the gerund.

options: She is going to get dressed quickly.
a2-09.why: Vestirse (reflexive) means to get dressed: the se refers back to Daniela. Dressing someone else would be vistió a alguien, se vio would be 'saw herself', and se vistió is preterite, not future.

a2-09.q: Mrs. Ortega says to Daniela in the interview: 'Llega tarde.' What does the verb form show?
options: It is a command to arrive.
Usted is used (formal), with the he/she verb form.
Tú is used (informal); llega is the tú form.
a2-09.why: Formal usted takes the he/she verb form (llega, tiene). With tú it would be llegas, tienes. Mrs. Ortega uses usted with Daniela throughout the interview.

a2-09.q: Mrs. Ortega tells Daniela: 'El puesto es suyo.' What does suyo mean here?
a2-09.why: With usted, the possessive is suyo/suya: el puesto es suyo = the job is yours. Context shows she is talking to Daniela.

a2-09.q: Fill in the blank: Mrs. Ortega asks Daniela (usted): ¿Ha ___ antes con clientes?
a2-09.why: Present perfect = haber + participle (-ado/-ido); with usted, haber is ha. The participle doesn't change for gender (not trabajada), trabajando is the gerund, and trabajo is the present.

a2-09.q: What is the difference between 'Daniela se despertó' and 'Daniela despertó a su hermana'?
options: Both mean that Daniela woke up.
The first: she woke up; the second: she woke her sister up.
The first: she woke her sister up; the second: she woke up.
The first is present, the second is past.
a2-09.why: With se the action falls back on the subject: se despertó = she woke up. Without se the verb takes an object: despertó a su hermana = she woke her sister up. Both are preterite.

a2-09.q: The older woman asks with tú: '¿Sabes dónde está la oficina?' How would she ask with usted?
a2-09.why: Usted uses the he/she form: (usted) sabe. Sabes is the tú form, and sabéis is vosotros (plural, Spain).

a2-09.q: Fill in the blank: La señora mayor entró en la sala y ___ junto a la jefa.
a2-09.why: Sentarse (to sit down) is reflexive, and the story tells finished events in the preterite: se sentó.

a2-10.q: Which sentence means 'It's the biggest lantern in the village'?
options: Es el farol más grande que el pueblo.
Es farol el más grande en pueblo.
Es el farol más grande del pueblo.
Es el farol grande más del pueblo.
a2-10.why: The superlative is el + noun + más + adjective + de (del = de + el), where English uses 'in'.

a2-10.topic: Perfect tenses: he visto, había aprendido
a2-10.q: Fill in the blank: Cuando Dolores llegó al granero, la lluvia ya ___ el papel.
a2-10.why: The rain soaked the paper before another past moment (when Dolores arrived), so use the past perfect: había + participle. Ha mojado connects to now, not to a past moment.

a2-10.q: Fill in the blank (that year): ___ año, Dolores tenía una misión especial.
a2-10.why: Año is masculine, so 'that' is ese. Esa and esta are feminine, and esto is neuter (not used before a noun).

a2-10.q: Why does the story say 'aquella fue la mejor noche de su vida'?
options: Aquella is for things close to the speaker.
Aquella points to a night far back in time.
a2-10.why: Aquel/aquella = that (far away), often for a moment in the distant past. Este/esta is for near things or now.

a2-10.q: Fill in the blanks: Después de la lluvia, el toro era ___ bonito ___ antes.
a2-10.why: To compare two things: más + adjective + que. Más de is used before numbers (más de cien personas), and tan pairs with como.

a2-10.topic: Perfect tenses: he visto, había aprendido
options: Nunca he veído trabajar tan rápido a este pueblo.
Nunca visto he trabajar tan rápido a este pueblo.
Nunca he visto trabajar tan rápido a este pueblo.
Nunca he vista trabajar tan rápido a este pueblo.
a2-10.why: Ver has an irregular participle, visto, which never changes for gender; he and the participle always stay together.
Demonstratives agree with the noun: este pueblo (m.), esta vez (f.), aquella noche (f.).

a2-10.q: Fill in the blank: Es la fiesta más importante ___ pueblo.
a2-10.why: In superlatives Spanish uses de where English says 'in': la fiesta más importante del pueblo.

b1-01.q: Complete: Cuando Inés ___ al hostal veinte minutos después, un joven ___ con la dueña desde hacía un rato.
b1-01.why: Llegó is the next event in the sequence (veinte minutos después). Hablaba is a conversation already in progress (desde hacía un rato), so it is background.

b1-01.q: Inés, a madrileña, is talking about this morning: «Esta mañana ___ una cartera en el Retiro.»
b1-01.why: In Spain, a time that includes today (esta mañana) takes the present perfect. Encontraba is background, había encontrado needs a later past moment, encontraría means 'would find'.

b1-01.q: Complete: Gustavo explicó que su abuela ___ a Chile muchos años antes.
b1-01.why: Muchos años antes points to an action finished before explicó, so the pluperfect: se había marchado. Se marcharía would put her departure after the explanation.

b1-01.q: Put into the past: «Es una mañana fría. Inés pasea por el Retiro cuando de repente ve algo verde.»
options: Era una mañana fría. Inés paseó por el Retiro cuando de repente vio algo verde.
Era una mañana fría. Inés paseaba por el Retiro cuando de repente veía algo verde.
Era una mañana fría. Inés había paseado por el Retiro cuando de repente vio algo verde.
Era una mañana fría. Inés paseaba por el Retiro cuando de repente vio algo verde.
b1-01.why: The walk is in progress (paseaba) when one sudden event cuts in (vio). Cuando de repente never introduces background, and había paseado would end the walk first.

b1-01.q: Which sentence is NOT correct in any variety of Spanish?
b1-01.why: Ayer is a finished time, so it needs the preterite everywhere. Hoy encontré is normal in Latin America and common in Spain too.

options: Su abuela se había marchada a Chile cuando era niña.
Su abuela había se marchado a Chile cuando era niña.
Su abuela se había marchado a Chile cuando era niña.
Su abuela se habían marchado a Chile cuando era niña.
b1-01.why: The pronoun goes before había, había agrees with the subject (singular), and the participle after haber never changes: marchado.

b1-01.q: Inés tells Gustavo: «He venido en persona porque quería devolvérsela hoy mismo.» Why does she use he venido?
options: The visit happened many years ago
Venir has no preterite form in Spanish
She is from Spain, and the visit happened today (hoy mismo), a time that includes now
She is talking about a habit she had in the past
b1-01.why: In Spain the present perfect is used for a time that includes now (hoy, esta mañana). Vine exists, the visit is not long ago and it is not a habit.

b1-01.q: In «un joven pálido hablaba con la dueña y casi lloraba», why are hablaba and lloraba in the imperfect?
options: They are completed events that move the story on
They are polite forms for talking to the owner
They happened before another past action
They were already in progress when Inés arrived: background
b1-01.why: The imperfect describes what was going on when Inés walked in (background). Completed events take the preterite, and an earlier action would take the pluperfect.

b1-02.q: Complete Bruno's prediction (you will have): «El año que viene ___ más experiencia.»
b1-02.why: Tener has the irregular stem tendr- + -ás: tendrás (same for tú and vos). *Tenerás doesn't exist, tendrías means 'you would have', tuvieras is subjunctive.

b1-02.q: Complete Nélida's rule: «Si el pan ___ frío, el chivito está triste.»
b1-02.why: A real condition or general truth takes si + present indicative. Never the future or the present subjunctive after si, and a temporary state like frío takes estar.

b1-02.topic: Object pronoun order: se lo, te la
b1-02.q: The judge asks for the secret. Complete Nélida's answer (usted): «___ digo: leche, azúcar…»
b1-02.why: Indirect (to you) comes before direct (it), and le becomes se before lo: se lo digo. Le lo and lo le never occur; se le leaves out 'it'.

b1-02.topic: Object pronoun order: se lo, te la
b1-02.q: Bruno asks for the mayonnaise recipe. Nélida speaks to him with vos: «Si venís todos los jueves, a lo mejor ___ cuento.»
b1-02.why: Te (to you) goes before la (la receta, feminine). Lo doesn't agree with receta; se la would mean to him, her or usted, not vos.

b1-02.q: Find the mistake: «El sábado me levantaré a las cinco, iré a la feria y comprará el mejor lomo.»
b1-02.why: Agustina is speaking about herself, so all three verbs need the yo ending -é: compraré. Comprará means he, she or usted will buy.
The si-clause takes the present indicative (vos llevás = tú llevas); the result can be future. Future, conditional and present subjunctive never follow this si.

b1-02.topic: Object pronoun order: se lo, te la
b1-02.q: In Nélida's answer to the judge, «Se lo digo», who does se refer to?
b1-02.why: Se here is le (to you, usted) changed before lo; lo is the secret. It is not reflexive: 'I tell myself' would be me lo digo.

b1-02.q: Change ir a + infinitive into the simple future: «Vas a perder.»
b1-02.why: Perder is regular in the future: perder + -ás. Only some verbs drop a vowel (poder → podrás); perderé is 'I', perderías is the conditional.

b1-03.q: Complete Remedios's answer: «Un horno eléctrico no ___ el mismo pan.» (= wouldn't make)
b1-03.why: Hacer uses the irregular stem har- in the conditional, as in the future: haría. *Hacería doesn't exist, hará = will make, hacía = used to make.

b1-03.q: Complete: «El técnico ___ al mediodía y revisó el horno durante una hora.»
b1-03.why: A finished event in a chain of past actions (llegó… revisó) takes the preterite. Ha llegado links to now, *ha llegó mixes two forms, llegaba describes background.

b1-03.q: Complete: «Faltaban cinco días para el Día de Muertos, la época del año ___ La Espiga vendía más pan de muerto.»
b1-03.why: After a word for time (la época, el día, el año), use en que. Donde is for places, quien for people, and lo que refers to a whole idea.

b1-03.q: Complete: «La víspera del Día de Muertos, todos los pedidos ___ listos.» (= ready)
b1-03.why: Listo with estar means 'ready', a state at that moment. With ser (eran listos) it would mean the orders were clever.

b1-03.q: Find the mistake: «Con cuatro hornos, poderíamos entregar todos los pedidos y usted descansaría.»
b1-03.why: Poder loses the e of its infinitive in the future and conditional: podr- → podríamos. Descansaría is a regular conditional and is correct.

b1-03.q: Complete: «El lunes se rompió el horno y desde entonces no ___ pan.»
b1-03.why: Desde entonces covers a period that reaches now, so the present perfect is used, in Mexico too. Hacer has the irregular participle hecho (never *hacido).

b1-03.q: What does «Iván, que siempre había sido muy listo» tell us about Iván?
options: He was always ready on time
b1-03.why: Ser listo describes a quality of a person: clever. Estar listo would mean 'ready', and rich is ser rico.

options: Remedios vio a las personas quien esperaban con sonrisas.
Remedios vio a las personas esperaban con sonrisas.
Remedios vio a las personas que ellas esperaban con sonrisas.
Remedios vio a las personas que esperaban con sonrisas.
b1-03.why: Use que right after the noun, and don't repeat the subject (*que ellas). Que can never be left out, and quien isn't used directly after a noun without commas.

b1-04.topic: Impersonal se: se puede, se cura
b1-04.q: Complete don Silvestre's words: «Las noches son tan oscuras que ___ tocar el cielo.»
b1-04.why: Impersonal se + singular verb means 'you / people can'. El cielo is singular, so no plural; pueden alone means 'they can'; se goes before the conjugated verb.

b1-04.topic: Impersonal se: se puede, se cura
b1-04.q: Complete the general statement: «En el turno de noche ___ (cansarse) muy rápido.»
b1-04.why: Cansarse already has se, and Spanish can't stack two se. For a general statement use uno + se cansa. Uno cansa would mean 'one tires others out'.

b1-04.topic: Verb phrases: llevar + gerund, seguir, volver a
b1-04.q: Complete: «La luz de esa estrella salió hace miles de años y sigue ___.»
b1-04.why: Seguir + gerund means 'keep doing / still be doing': sigue llegando. Seguir is not followed by an infinitive, with or without a.

b1-04.q: Complete: «Hasta esa noche, Marcos nunca ___ la vista durante su turno.»
b1-04.why: Something that had not happened before a past moment (hasta esa noche) takes the pluperfect. The participle never agrees: levantado, not levantada.

b1-04.topic: Impersonal se: se puede, se cura
options: En este hospital se trabaja de noche.
Cuando uno se cae, tarda en recuperarse.
Cuando se se cae, se tarda mucho en recuperarse.
Desde esa ventana se puede ver Antares por la noche.
b1-04.why: Caerse already has se, so a general statement can't add another: cuando uno se cae. The other sentences use impersonal se correctly.

b1-04.topic: Verb phrases: llevar + gerund, seguir, volver a
b1-04.q: In which sentence does volver a mean 'again'?
options: Esa semana volvió a llamar a su hermana.
Volvió al hospital a las diez.
Al día siguiente podría volver a su casa.
b1-04.why: Volver a + infinitive (llamar) means 'do again'. Volver a + a place (su casa, la habitación) simply means 'go back to'.

b1-04.topic: Verb phrases: llevar + gerund, seguir, volver a
b1-04.q: Rewrite with llevar + gerund: «Marcos vive en Santiago desde hace diez años.»
options: Marcos lleva diez años viviendo en Santiago.
Marcos lleva diez años vivido en Santiago.
Marcos está diez años viviendo en Santiago.
Marcos lleva vivir diez años en Santiago.
b1-04.why: Llevar + time + gerund (viviendo) says how long an action has been going on. It needs the gerund, not a participle or infinitive, and estar can't replace llevar.

b1-04.q: Which sentence is correct? (My grandmother fell before she went into hospital.)
options: Mi abuela había se caído en la calle.
Mi abuela se había caída en la calle.
Mi abuela se había caído en la calle.
Mi abuela había caídose en la calle.
b1-04.why: The pronoun goes before había, and the participle stays in -o even with a female subject: se había caído.

b1-05.q: Complete from the story: «Leticia se había enojado con él ___ la venta de la casa de sus padres.»
b1-05.why: Por gives the cause or reason ('over, because of'). Para would make the sale the goal of her anger.

b1-05.q: Complete don Walter's words: «Si pudiera hablar con él una hora más, solo le ___ que me alegro de haber crecido a su lado.»
b1-05.why: An imagined situation takes the conditional: decir → diría (future stem). Decía is a past habit, dirá a real future.

b1-05.q: Don Walter: «Perdí a mi hermano en una tormenta.» Complete the narration: «El hombre les contó que ___ a su propio hermano.»
b1-05.why: After a past verb (contó), an earlier event goes into the pluperfect, and the person changes: perdí → había perdido.

b1-05.topic: Connectors: por eso, así que, a pesar de
b1-05.q: Complete Nicolás's words: «Papá siempre decía que si uno quiere llegar lejos, tiene que prepararse para lo peor. ___ traje uno para ti.»
b1-05.why: Así que ('so') introduces the result of what came before: because of Dad's advice, he brought a spare. A pesar de and aunque express contrast, and para que expresses purpose.

b1-05.q: Complete: «Salieron de Manta un lunes ___ la mañana ___ llegar a Montañita en una semana.»
b1-05.why: Por la mañana marks a part of the day. Para + infinitive gives the purpose: in order to reach Montañita.

b1-05.q: Which sentence correctly says 'When they were kids, Dad would always tell them stories about the sea'?
options: De niños, papá siempre les contaría historias del mar.
De niños, papá siempre les contaba historias del mar.
De niños, papá siempre les contará historias del mar.
De niños, papá siempre les ha contado historias del mar.
b1-05.why: Here 'would' means 'used to': a repeated past habit takes the imperfect (contaba). The conditional contaría is for imagined situations.

b1-05.q: Transform into reported speech. Tía Yolanda: «El mejor camino para volver a alguien es el que se hace juntos.» → Leticia: «Tía Yolanda dijo…»
options: el mejor camino es el que se hace juntos.
de que el mejor camino es el que se hace juntos.
que el mejor camino es el que se hace juntos.
si el mejor camino es el que se hace juntos.
b1-05.why: Decir + que + statement. Que can't be dropped, decir de que is a common error, and si is only for reported yes/no questions.

b1-05.topic: Connectors: por eso, así que, a pesar de
b1-05.q: Complete: «Cuando por fin vieron el cartel de Montañita, ___ agotados y quemados por el sol, ninguno quería que el viaje terminara.»
b1-05.why: They didn't want the trip to end even though they were exhausted: that is contrast, so a pesar de + infinitive. Por eso and así que introduce a result, and para gives a purpose.

b1-06.q: Ximena hopes the daughter will write back. Complete: Espero que la hija de Octavio me ___ pronto.
b1-06.why: Espero que + a different subject takes the present subjunctive: (ella) conteste. Contesta is indicative, the infinitive needs the same subject, and contestes is the tú form.

b1-06.q: Complete: Creo que la abuela ___ feliz con las cartas, pero no creo que ___ dormir esta noche.
b1-06.why: Creo que states a belief, so indicative (estará). No creo que expresses doubt, so subjunctive (pueda).

b1-06.q: Marisol tells her cousin (tú): 'Don't tell her anything.'
b1-06.why: Negative tú command = no + present subjunctive: digas (from digo). Pronoun before the verb. No le dices is a statement; dile is only affirmative.

b1-06.q: Rocío's father saw the photo a few minutes ago. Complete: «Mi padre ___ ver esta foto.»
b1-06.why: Acabar de + infinitive means 'to have just done something': acaba de ver = has just seen. The de can't be dropped, and deja de means 'stops'.

options: Es importante que no se hace ilusiones.
b1-06.why: Es importante que is a value judgement and needs the subjunctive: se haga. Creo que (belief) correctly takes the indicative.

b1-06.q: Make the command negative: «Dile la verdad.» → «___ la verdad.»
b1-06.why: In a negative command the pronoun moves in front and the verb becomes subjunctive: dile → no le digas.

b1-06.q: What does «Por orgullo dejé de preguntar por él» mean?
options: Out of pride I kept asking about him.
Out of pride I stopped asking about him.
Out of pride I let him ask about me.
Out of pride I had just asked about him.
b1-06.why: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something': dejé de preguntar = I stopped asking. 'Had just asked' would be acababa de preguntar.

b1-06.q: Which sentence correctly says 'Marisol hopes to find more letters'?
options: Marisol espera que encuentra más cartas.
Marisol espera que encuentre más cartas.
Marisol espera a encontrar más cartas.
b1-06.why: Same subject (Marisol hopes, Marisol finds) → infinitive. Que + subjunctive means someone else will find them.

b1-07.q: Camilo speaks to the three investors (ustedes). Complete: «___ que van caminando por una ciudad que no conocen.»
b1-07.why: Ustedes commands use the present subjunctive: imaginen. Imaginan is a statement, imagina is tú, and the infinitive doesn't address people.

b1-07.q: Teresa to the investors: «Si ustedes prefieren que nosotros ___, lo entenderemos.»
b1-07.why: Two different subjects (ustedes prefieren / nosotros nos vamos), so preferir que takes the present subjunctive: nos vayamos. The infinitive works only with one subject.

b1-07.topic: Subjunctive after para que, antes de que
b1-07.q: Complete Teresa's advice: «Habla despacio para que te ___.»
b1-07.why: Para que always takes the subjunctive, because the purpose is not a fact yet: entiendan. Entienden and entenderán state facts.

b1-07.topic: Subjunctive after para que, antes de que
b1-07.q: Camilo himself will give the talk. Complete: «Camilo ensaya cada noche ___ bien la presentación.»
b1-07.why: Same subject in both parts (Camilo ensaya, Camilo hace), so use para + infinitive. Para que + subjunctive is for a different subject.

b1-07.q: Camilo's mother speaks to him as tú. Which of her messages contains a mistake?
options: ¡Llama a tu abuela, que te extraña mucho!
b1-07.why: Negative tú commands use the present subjunctive, built on the yo form salgo: no salgas. No sales is a statement ('you don't go out').

b1-07.topic: Subjunctive after para que, antes de que
b1-07.q: Teresa: «Vuelve ya, antes de que cambien de opinión.» What does she mean?
options: The investors have already changed their minds.
Come back now: they haven't changed their minds yet, but they might.
Come back when they change their minds.
Come back, because the investors always change their minds at the end.
b1-07.why: Antes de que + subjunctive refers to something that hasn't happened yet and may not happen. A fact would need porque + indicative.

b1-07.topic: Subjunctive after para que, antes de que
b1-07.q: Join the two ideas with para que: «Camilo habla despacio. Los inversionistas lo entienden.»
options: Camilo habla despacio para que los inversionistas pueden entenderlo.
Camilo habla despacio para que los inversionistas lo entienden.
Camilo habla despacio para los inversionistas entenderlo.
Camilo habla despacio para que los inversionistas lo entiendan.
b1-07.why: Different subjects, so para que + subjunctive: lo entiendan. Para + infinitive is only for the same subject, and para que never takes the indicative or an infinitive.

b1-07.q: How does Camilo's mother say 'I want you to call your grandmother'?
options: Quiero a ti llamar a tu abuela.
Quiero que llames a tu abuela.
Quiero que llamas a tu abuela.
b1-07.why: 'Want you to' becomes querer que + subjunctive: llames. Quiero llamar means 'I want to call', and que can't be dropped.

b1-08.q: Complete: «Si no ___ por usted, hoy no sería ingeniera.»
b1-08.why: Unreal condition: si + imperfect subjunctive (fuera), then the conditional in the result (sería). The conditional never goes after si.

b1-08.q: Complete the result: «Si Aurelio se quedara en casa, ___ tiempo para leer todos sus libros.»
b1-08.why: After si + imperfect subjunctive, the result is conditional: tendría. Tendrá pairs with si + present (real condition); tuviera belongs in the si part.

b1-08.q: Complete: «Mañana, cuando Aurelio ___ al centro comunitario, los niños lo estarán esperando.»
b1-08.why: Cuando refers to a future moment (mañana), so it takes the present subjunctive: llegue. Spanish never uses the future after cuando.

b1-08.topic: Relative clauses: donde, que, lo que
b1-08.q: Complete: «Pero ___ más lo desconcertó fue ver a decenas de adultos al fondo.»
b1-08.why: There is no noun before the relative, and it means 'the thing that / what', so Spanish uses lo que. A bare que needs a noun before it.

options: Si tuviera tiempo, leería todos esos libros.
Si Carmen lo invita, él irá los sábados.
Si no fuera por usted, no sería ingeniera.
Si volvería a empezar, elegiría otra vez esta escuela.
b1-08.why: The conditional can't follow si: it should be si volviera. Si + present + future (last option) is a correct real condition.

b1-08.q: «Hagan preguntas, aunque les dé vergüenza.» What does aunque + subjunctive mean here?
options: even if you may feel embarrassed
b1-08.why: With the subjunctive, aunque presents a possibility ('even if'). With the indicative (aunque les da vergüenza) it states a fact ('although').

b1-08.topic: Relative clauses: donde, que, lo que
b1-08.q: Join the two sentences: «Aurelio caminó por el pasillo. En el pasillo había murales de colores.»
options: Aurelio caminó por el pasillo, lo que había murales.
Aurelio caminó por el pasillo, que había murales de colores.
Aurelio caminó por el pasillo, donde había murales de colores.
Aurelio caminó por el pasillo, quien había murales de colores.
b1-08.why: After a place, 'where' is donde (or en el que). Que alone can't replace en el pasillo, and quien is only for people.

b1-08.q: Gap-fill: «Cuando yo ___ joven, no entendía a mi profesor. Tú también lo entenderás cuando ___ mayor.»
b1-08.why: Cuando + indicative for the past (era); cuando + subjunctive for the future (seas). The tense of the main verb tells you which.

b1-09.q: Doña Rosa gritaba: «¡No usen el ascensor!» Complete the report: Doña Rosa gritaba que no ___ el ascensor.
b1-09.why: A reported command after a past verb (gritaba) needs que + imperfect subjunctive: usaran. Usaban would report a fact, not an order.

b1-09.q: Complete: Doña Rosa nos pide que ___ con cuidado por las escaleras.
b1-09.why: Pedir que + subjunctive. The reporting verb is present (pide), so the present subjunctive follows: bajemos. Que can't be followed by an infinitive.

b1-09.topic: Accidental se: se le olvidó, se le acabó
b1-09.q: Soledad didn't mean to forget. Complete: «Se le ___ guardar el archivo.»
b1-09.why: In accidental se the verb agrees with what is forgotten. An infinitive (guardar el archivo) counts as singular, so se le olvidó. Le shows who it happened to.

b1-09.topic: Verbs of change: ponerse, quedarse, convertirse
b1-09.q: Complete: Después de cenar, Gonzalo se ___ dormido sobre las piernas de su madre.
b1-09.why: Quedarse + participle or adjective describes the state that results: quedarse dormido = fall asleep. Ponerse and volverse don't go with dormido; convertirse needs en + noun.

b1-09.q: In which sentence does the verb report an order, not a piece of information?
options: Gonzalo decía que la oscuridad le daba miedo.
Gutiérrez contó que su esposa había fallecido.
La compañía eléctrica dice que el apagón puede durar toda la noche.
Soledad le dijo que no tuviera miedo.
b1-09.why: Decir que + subjunctive (tuviera) reports a command: 'told him not to be afraid'. With the indicative (daba, había fallecido, puede) it only reports information.

b1-09.topic: Accidental se: se le olvidó, se le acabó
b1-09.q: The computer's battery ran out. Which sentence is correct?
options: A la computadora le se acabó la batería.
A la computadora se le acabó la batería.
A la computadora se le acabaron la batería.
La computadora se acabó la batería.
b1-09.why: The order is se + le + verb, and the verb agrees with la batería (singular): se le acabó. Le se is never correct.

b1-09.topic: Verbs of change: ponerse, quedarse, convertirse
options: El cielo se puso negro y el vestíbulo se convirtió en un comedor.
El cielo se puso negro y el vestíbulo se convirtió un comedor.
El cielo se convirtió negro y el vestíbulo se puso un comedor.
El cielo se puso en negro y el vestíbulo se quedó un comedor.
b1-09.why: Ponerse + adjective for a sudden change (se puso negro); convertirse en + noun for a transformation. Without en, convertirse is wrong.

b1-09.topic: Accidental se: se le olvidó, se le acabó
b1-09.q: What does «Se me va a descongelar el congelador» tell us about Gutiérrez?
options: He wants to defrost the freezer on purpose.
Someone else is going to defrost his freezer.
He has already defrosted the freezer.
The freezer is going to defrost and it isn't his fault.
b1-09.why: Se me + verb presents something as an accident that happens to the speaker: the blackout, not Gutiérrez, is defrosting the freezer.

b1-10.q: Complete: En Antigua, las alfombras de Viernes Santo se ___ con aserrín de colores.
b1-10.why: Passive se agrees with the thing: las alfombras is plural, so se hacen. Se hace is the classic slip; hecho needs ser or estar.

b1-10.q: Itzel is wondering about the clue. Complete her question: ¿Y qué ___ «la mano que toca»?
b1-10.why: To wonder or guess about the present, Spanish uses the future: ¿qué será? = what can it be? Sea and fuera are subjunctive forms with no trigger, and seré is the yo form.

b1-10.q: Complete: Bayron e Itzel caminaron ___ la calle del arco ___ buscar la casa.
b1-10.why: Por marks the path (along the street); para + infinitive marks the purpose (in order to look for).

b1-10.q: Complete: Construyeron el arco ___ que las monjas pudieran cruzar la calle sin ser vistas.
b1-10.why: Purpose with a new subject is para que + subjunctive (pudieran). Porque gives a cause and takes the indicative; por que is not a purpose link.

b1-10.q: Find the mistake: «En Antigua se ve muchas puertas con aldabas de bronce.»
b1-10.why: Puertas is plural, so the se verb must be plural too: se ven. Singular se ve only fits a singular noun or a verb with no noun.

b1-10.q: In which sentence does the future express a guess, not a future event?
options: Si caminamos por esa calle, encontraremos la casa.
Si tienes suerte, esta noche verás la lava.
Si vuelves el año que viene, iré contigo.
b1-10.why: ¿Será alguien…? wonders about the present ('could it be someone…?'). The other sentences talk about real future events.

b1-10.q: What does «Por eso la llamamos Antigua» mean?
options: That's why we call it Antigua.
We call it Antigua for that purpose.
We call it Antigua through that.
b1-10.why: Por eso looks back at a cause: 'that's why'. Para eso would mean 'for that purpose', which isn't what Bayron means.

options: Las alfombras no se hace para durar.
Las alfombras no se hacen por durar.
Las alfombras no hacen para durar.
Las alfombras no se hacen para durar.
b1-10.why: Plural noun, plural se verb (se hacen), and purpose is para + infinitive. Without se, 'the carpets don't make' makes no sense.

b2-01.topic: Subjunctive after conjunctions (para que, sin que, antes de que...)
b2-01.q: Complete: «Ignacio dejó el sobre en la tapa para que otro archivista lo ___ algún día.»
b2-01.why: Para que always takes the subjunctive; after a past main verb (dejó), the imperfect subjunctive: encontrara. The conditional and the indicative cannot follow para que.

b2-01.q: Ignacio has no idea whether Elvira will remember Facundo. He decides: «Iré a verla aunque no ___ a Facundo.»
b2-01.why: He doesn't know, so the clause is only a possibility, 'even if she doesn't remember': subjunctive. Recuerda or recordará would state it as something he knows.

b2-01.q: The narrator reports a fact about Ignacio's feelings: «Rasgó el borde del sobre, aunque ___ un poco culpable.»
b2-01.why: The narrator asserts a real feeling, so aunque takes the indicative; imperfect because it is background. Se sintiera would turn it into a mere possibility.

b2-01.q: Complete Adriana's offer: «Pues si usted me ___, yo podría buscar en los registros civiles.»
b2-01.why: An unlikely condition with a conditional result (podría) needs si + imperfect subjunctive. *Si dejaría copies English 'if you would'; si never takes the present subjunctive.

b2-01.topic: Subjunctive after conjunctions (para que, sin que, antes de que...)
options: Elvira leyó la carta sin que le temblara la voz.
Ignacio escondió el sobre antes de que llegó su jefe.
Facundo prometió esperarla hasta que terminara el invierno.
Adriana buscó en los periódicos para que Ignacio no tuviera que salir.
b2-01.why: Antes de que always takes the subjunctive, even for an event that really happened: antes de que llegara. The other three conjunctions are correctly followed by the subjunctive.

b2-01.q: Rewrite so it means 'even if': «Aunque Adriana tiene poco tiempo, ayudará a Ignacio.»
options: Aunque Adriana tiene poco tiempo, ayudaría a Ignacio.
Aunque Adriana tendría poco tiempo, ayudará a Ignacio.
Aunque Adriana tuvo poco tiempo, ayudará a Ignacio.
Aunque Adriana tenga poco tiempo, ayudará a Ignacio.
b2-01.why: Switching to the subjunctive (tenga) turns a stated fact into a possibility: 'even if she has little time'. Changing the main verb does not change the meaning of aunque.

options: Si Ignacio tendría tiempo, buscaría a Elvira.
Si Ignacio tuviera tiempo, buscará a Elvira.
Si Ignacio tenga tiempo, buscaría a Elvira.
Si Ignacio tuviera tiempo, buscaría a Elvira.
b2-01.why: Hypothetical pattern: si + imperfect subjunctive, conditional. Si never takes the conditional or the present subjunctive, and tuviera does not combine with a future result.

b2-01.topic: Subjunctive after conjunctions (para que, sin que, antes de que...)
b2-01.q: Join with sin que: «Elvira leyó la carta. Nadie la interrumpió.»
options: Elvira leyó la carta sin que nadie la interrumpió.
Elvira leyó la carta sin que nadie la interrumpiera.
Elvira leyó la carta sin que nadie la interrumpa.
Elvira leyó la carta sin nadie la interrumpiera.
b2-01.why: Sin que needs both words and the subjunctive; after a past verb (leyó), the imperfect subjunctive: interrumpiera. The indicative interrumpió is the typical mistake.

b2-02.q: Complete: «Por mucho que los clientes ___ (protestar) el viernes, Esperanza va a estrenar la carta nueva.»
b2-02.why: Por mucho que takes the subjunctive; the protest is still to come (el viernes, va a estrenar), so present subjunctive. The future never follows por mucho que.

b2-02.topic: Verb phrases: seguir, acabar + gerund; soler
b2-02.q: Complete Esperanza's warning (would end up closing): «Si siguiéramos haciendo siempre lo mismo, el negocio acabaría ___.»
b2-02.why: Acabar + gerund means 'end up doing'. Acabar de + infinitive means 'have just done', and *acabar cerrar / *acabar a cerrar are not Spanish.

b2-02.topic: Subjunctive after no es que, temer que, a que
b2-02.q: Complete don Leandro's reply: «No es que no me ___ (gustar) la carta nueva, hija; es que aquí la gente quiere lo de siempre.»
b2-02.why: No es que denies a reason, so the verb goes in the subjunctive: guste. The real reason, introduced by es que, stays in the indicative: quiere.

b2-02.topic: Subjunctive after no es que, temer que, a que
b2-02.q: Complete: «Aquí la gente no viene a que le ___ (explicar) la comida.»
b2-02.why: Venir a que + subjunctive gives the purpose with a new subject (they explain). The main verb viene is present, so present subjunctive: expliquen.

b2-02.q: What does the subjunctive suggest in «Y su padre, aunque no lo diga, lo anota en la libreta de ventas con un asterisco»?
options: Whether he says it or not doesn't matter: his note shows he approves.
He has never noticed the special dish.
He may start saying it openly soon.
He tells everyone he is proud of it.
b2-02.why: Aunque + subjunctive presents the concession as irrelevant to the point. Aunque no lo dice would simply report, as new information, that he doesn't say it.

b2-02.topic: Verb phrases: seguir, acabar + gerund; soler
options: Doña Chela suele sentarse en la misma mesa.
Al final, el negocio acabó cerrando.
Esperanza siguió cocinando en el pib.
La abuela solió decir que la paciencia no se compra.
b2-02.why: Soler is used only in the present and imperfect: 'used to say' is solía decir. Seguir and acabar + gerund work in any tense.

b2-02.topic: Subjunctive after no es que, temer que, a que
options: No es que sea terco; es que está asustado.
No es que es terco; es que esté asustado.
No es que sea terco; es que esté asustado.
No es que es terco; es que está asustado.
b2-02.why: No es que (rejected reason) takes the subjunctive; es que (real reason) takes the indicative. Mixing them up, in either half, is the typical error.

b2-02.topic: Subjunctive after no es que, temer que, a que
b2-02.q: Put into the past: «Los clientes tienen miedo de que Esperanza cambie la carta.» → «Aquel viernes, los clientes tenían miedo de que Esperanza ___ la carta.»
b2-02.why: Tener miedo de que always takes the subjunctive; with a past main verb about a past event, use the imperfect subjunctive: cambiara.

b2-03.q: Complete: «Al principio, Begoña miraba a los peregrinos como si ___ turistas en un parque temático.»
b2-03.why: Como si always takes the subjunctive, imperfect for the same time: fueran. The indicative (eran), the conditional (serían) and the present subjunctive (sean) are never used after como si.

b2-03.q: Complete with the ser passive: «El Pórtico de la Gloria ___ por el Maestro Mateo en el siglo XII.»
b2-03.why: Ser + participle agreeing with el Pórtico (masculine singular), with por for the agent. Estar gives a state, not the action; esculpiendo is a gerund.

b2-03.q: Complete: «Aquella mañana, Xosé les pidió que ___ el Pórtico antes de la misa.»
b2-03.why: Pedir que + subjunctive, and the request is past (pidió, aquella mañana), so imperfect subjunctive: vieran. The indicative and the conditional don't follow a request.

b2-03.q: Complete: «Begoña cargó con la mochila verde hasta Ribadiso para que Rosendo no ___ que buscarla.»
b2-03.why: Para que with a different subject always takes the subjunctive. The main verb (cargó) is past and the purpose is completed, so the imperfect subjunctive: tuviera.

b2-03.q: Find the mistake: «Rosendo hablaba del cuaderno como si Amparo todavía caminaba a su lado.»
options: como si should be como que
b2-03.why: After como si the verb must be in the subjunctive: como si caminara. The main verb hablaba is a normal imperfect indicative and stays.

b2-03.q: Rewrite with the ser passive: «Ocho hombres impulsan el botafumeiro.»
options: El botafumeiro se impulsa por ocho hombres.
El botafumeiro es impulsado por ocho hombres.
El botafumeiro está impulsando por ocho hombres.
El botafumeiro es impulsada por ocho hombres.
b2-03.why: Ser + participle agreeing with el botafumeiro (masculine): es impulsado, with por for the agent. Passive se doesn't take a por-agent.

options: Se vendían conchas a las puertas de la catedral.
Se vendía conchas a las puertas de la catedral.
Conchas fueron vendido a las puertas de la catedral.
Se vendían conchas por los comerciantes.
b2-03.why: Passive se agrees with the noun (conchas, plural: se vendían) and names no agent. A ser passive needs an agreeing participle (vendidas).

b2-03.q: Compare «Rosendo le dijo que escribiera ella la entrada» with «Rosendo le dijo que escribía ella la entrada». What does the second one mean?
options: Rosendo told her that she was the one writing the entry: information, not a request.
Rosendo would write the entry later.
Rosendo told her to write the entry.
Rosendo hoped she would write the entry.
b2-03.why: Decir que + subjunctive reports an order or request; decir que + indicative reports information. Escribiera = told her to write; escribía = said she was writing.

b2-04.topic: Indicative vs subjunctive: opinion, doubt and emotion
b2-04.q: Complete: «Whitcombe no esperaba que una traductora desconocida le ___ esa pregunta.»
b2-04.why: No esperaba que expresses (failed) expectation, so subjunctive; the trigger is past, so imperfect subjunctive: hiciera. Haga would need a present trigger (no espero que).

b2-04.topic: Discourse markers: sin embargo, en cambio, en cuanto a
b2-04.q: Complete: «En inglés la ambigüedad era un recurso elegante; el español, ___, la obligaba a decidirse.»
b2-04.why: En cambio contrasts two different things (English vs Spanish). A cambio means 'in exchange', en cuanto 'as soon as', por lo tanto 'therefore'.

b2-04.topic: Ojalá and como si with pluperfect
b2-04.q: Complete Whitcombe's regret: «Ojalá yo ___ esa libertad hace veinticinco años.»
b2-04.why: Regret about a past that can't change: ojalá + pluperfect subjunctive. Tuviera is a wish about now; haya tenido hopes about an unknown past outcome.

b2-04.topic: Mixed conditionals: si hubiera…, ahora sería
b2-04.q: Ramiro is asking Maribel right now to soften the sentence. Complete her reply: «Si hubieras leído el correo del autor, no me ___ lo contrario.»
b2-04.why: The condition is in the past (hubieras leído) but the result is happening now, so the main clause takes the simple conditional: pedirías. The subjunctive cannot be the result clause, and the preterite and future don't express an unreal result.

b2-04.topic: Indicative vs subjunctive: opinion, doubt and emotion
b2-04.q: Whitcombe writes «Me temo que la frase significa exactamente lo que usted sospecha». What does me temo que do here?
options: It expresses fear about something that may still happen.
It politely introduces an unwelcome fact, so the indicative follows.
It shows that he doubts Maribel's reading, so significa should be signifique.
It is an order not to change the sentence.
b2-04.why: Me temo que works like English 'I'm afraid that': it softens news the speaker knows is true, so it takes the indicative, unlike temer que expressing real fear.

b2-04.topic: Discourse markers: sin embargo, en cambio, en cuanto a
options: La embajada, por su parte, no hizo ningún comentario sobre la nota.
Sin embargo que el plazo era corto, terminó a tiempo.
En cuanto a ella, aprendió una lección.
Aquel libro, sin embargo, avanzaba con fluidez.
b2-04.why: Sin embargo links two separate clauses and never takes que. Say Aunque el plazo era corto, … or El plazo era corto; sin embargo, terminó a tiempo.

b2-04.topic: Ojalá and como si with pluperfect
options: Se sintió como si le habían confiado una carga.
Me miró como si yo habría mentido.
Me habla como si me conozca desde hace muchísimos años.
Se sintió como si le hubieran confiado una carga.
b2-04.why: Como si takes only the imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive. The conditional, the present subjunctive and the indicative are not possible after it.

b2-04.topic: Mixed conditionals: si hubiera…, ahora sería
b2-04.q: Which sentence means 'If she had not received that letter, she would be a different translator today'?
options: Si no recibiera aquella carta, hoy habría sido una traductora distinta.
Si no habría recibido aquella carta, hoy sería una traductora distinta.
Si no había recibido aquella carta, hoy es una traductora distinta.
Si no hubiera recibido aquella carta, hoy sería una traductora distinta.
b2-04.why: Past condition (pluperfect subjunctive hubiera recibido) + present result (conditional sería, with hoy). The conditional never goes after si, and the indicative había recibido does not express an unreal past.

b2-05.q: Complete Mercedes's reasoning: «Si a las seis y cuarto ___, Bernardo habría vuelto empapado antes de las siete.»
b2-05.why: An unreal past condition takes the pluperfect subjunctive after si. Habría never follows si, había estado lloviendo states a fact, and llovería is about the present or future.

b2-05.q: Ugarte on the phone: «Estoy aquí desde el viernes y el lunes estaré en la librería.» Complete the narration: «Dijo que ___ allí desde el viernes y que el lunes ___ en la librería.»
b2-05.why: After dijo, present estoy becomes imperfect estaba and future estaré becomes conditional estaría. The Monday is past for the narrator, so estará doesn't fit.

b2-05.q: Don Aníbal to Tobías at six: «Bajá (= baja) al sótano a ordenar revistas.» Tobías tells Mercedes: «Tu abuelo me dijo que ___ al sótano.»
b2-05.why: A reported command after a past verb takes que + imperfect subjunctive. Bajaba would report a fact, not an order; dijo bajar and bajaría are learner errors.

b2-05.q: Nobody actually offered Don Aníbal three times the price. Complete: «Aunque me ___ el triple, no lo habría vendido.»
b2-05.why: An imagined past offer that wouldn't have changed anything: aunque + pluperfect subjunctive. Ofrecieron or habían ofrecido would say the offer really happened.

b2-05.q: Find the error: «Si me habrías preguntado, te hubiera dicho que hay cosas que no se venden.»
options: te hubiera dicho → te habría dicho
no se venden → no se vende
b2-05.why: The si-clause needs the pluperfect subjunctive. In the result clause, hubiera dicho is as correct as habría dicho.

b2-05.q: Mercedes asked Tobías: «¿Y no oíste la campanita de la puerta?» Transform: «Mercedes le preguntó a Tobías ___ la campanita.»
b2-05.why: A reported yes/no question is introduced by si, and the preterite shifts to the pluperfect. Habría oído would be a hypothetical, not a report.

b2-05.q: Ugarte: «Aunque me lo hubieran regalado, jamás lo habría sacado a la calle con lluvia.» What does he mean?
options: He wishes someone had given him the book.
Even as a gift, he would never have taken it out in the rain.
Someone really gave him the book as a present, so he kept it safe at home.
He took it out because it was a gift.
b2-05.why: Aunque + pluperfect subjunctive imagines a past that didn't happen and says the result would be the same. It's his proof that he isn't the thief.

b2-05.q: Mercedes regrets her promise to Ugarte. Which sentence is correct?
options: Ojalá no se lo hubiera prometido.
Ojalá no se lo habría prometido.
Ojalá no se lo había prometido.
Ojalá que no se lo he prometido.
b2-05.why: A regret about the past is ojalá + pluperfect subjunctive. Ojalá never takes the conditional, and the indicative forms don't express a regret.

b2-06.q: Complete: «Cuando la aprendiz abrió el cajón, el reloj todavía ___ parado a las cuatro y diez.»
b2-06.why: The watch is in a state that resulted from stopping, so estar + participle; todavía and the background description call for the imperfect: estaba.

b2-06.q: The apprentice thought: «No haré nada irreparable.» Complete the report: «Me dije que no ___ nada irreparable.»
b2-06.why: A future seen from a past reporting verb becomes the conditional: haré → haría. Hiciera would turn a statement into a request.

b2-06.topic: Subjunctive in time clauses: cuando, hasta que, mientras
b2-06.q: Complete: «Don Eusebio decidió que no tocaría el reloj hasta que la dueña ___.»
b2-06.why: Her return is still pending from the past viewpoint (decidió, tocaría), so hasta que takes the imperfect subjunctive. A conditional never follows hasta que.

b2-06.topic: Verb + preposition: depender de, pensar en
b2-06.q: Complete: «Una mañana de lluvia me atreví ___ preguntarle por el reloj, pero él se negaba ___ hablar de él.»
b2-06.why: Both verbs take a before an infinitive: atreverse a (dare to) and negarse a (refuse to). The preposition belongs to the verb, so learn them as a unit.

b2-06.q: Rewrite as the resulting state: «Alguien cerró el cajón con llave.» → «El cajón ___ con llave.»
b2-06.why: State = estar + participle agreeing with el cajón: estaba cerrado. Fue cerrado describes the action, not the state.

b2-06.topic: Subjunctive in time clauses: cuando, hasta que, mientras
b2-06.q: Choose the pair: «Mientras el maestro ___ en el entierro, abrí el cajón.» / «Mientras el reloj ___ parado (as long as), ella tendría un motivo para volver.»
b2-06.why: First: a real past fact, mientras = 'while', indicative estaba. Second: a condition, mientras = 'as long as', imperfect subjunctive estuviera.
